body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{low}}\) exhibit constants \(\eta\in(0,1-2\alpha)\), \(\varepsilon_R\in(0,\min\{R_f,R_q\})\), and \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\), and construct \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\in\mathcal M\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), with fixed \(p_x\), fixed positive \(f_x\), and fixed nonidentical asymmetric laws of \(U_1,U_2\) shared across \(j\in\{0,1\}\) and across \(n\), such that only the Bernoulli conditional means \(b_{j,n,x}\) differ; \(1/4\le b_{j,n,x}(a)\le3/4\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\); \(\sup_x\|f_x\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_f-\varepsilon_R\) and \(\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\sup_x\|f_xb_{j,n,x}\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_q-\varepsilon_R\); \(\operatorname{TV}(((P_{0,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},((P_{1,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le\eta\); and \(\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^{\infty}(I)}\ge c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}\)?
body.justification: The protected neighborhood and model nonemptiness are settled, but the strict-interior Bernoulli packet and product-experiment contiguity remain unresolved.
body.gap: Primitive compatibility allows \(R_q\le1/(4\sqrt{2B_A})\), whereas any packet with \(b\ge1/4\) requires a strictly larger marked Sobolev radius; even compatible interiors still need the new packet/Hellinger argument.
body.consumer: Only an affirmative resolution would activate the conditional all-band testing converse.

obligation.what_is_open: For fixed indices admitting strict Sobolev interior, construct one fixed positive density and fixed nonidentical asymmetric error pair together with Bernoulli marked perturbations satisfying the range and strict slack constraints, achieving \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) separation, and having product-experiment total variation below \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).
obligation.obstruction: The new primitive compatibility makes the full model and exact projected class nonempty, but it does not guarantee the strict interior required by this lower experiment; in particular the Bernoulli floor forces \(R_q>1/(4\sqrt{2B_A})\), while the class assumes only \(R_q>0\). Even in a strict-interior regime, the frozen primitives do not supply a moment-annihilating packet that simultaneously preserves the Bernoulli range and Sobolev slack or a weighted chi-square/Hellinger lower-envelope argument converting factorial Fourier attenuation into the required product total-variation bound.
obligation.attempted: The moment condition was used to obtain the protected neighborhood \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\), \(c_*=1/2\), and the new explicit reference law supplies fixed nonidentical asymmetric errors and a positive density. Moment annihilation was then carried through the marked-channel factorization to a factorial transform bound. These steps do not construct the required packet or control product Hellinger distance.
obligation.partial_result:
The moment condition supplies the protected neighborhood: by \(\mathrm{lem{:}moment\text{-}derived\text{-}local\text{-}modulus}\), every admissible error law satisfies
\[
 |\phi_Q(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e},
 \quad
 \inf_{|t|\le\nu_*}|\phi_Q(t)|\ge c_*,
 \quad
 \nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1},\quad c_*=\frac12.
\]
Thus no separate spectral-modulus restriction is needed.  The new compatibility condition and \(\mathrm{lem{:}model\text{-}class\text{-}nonempty}\) provide a fixed positive density and fixed nonidentical asymmetric errors in an inhabited full model.  They do not, however, guarantee the strict interior required by the lower experiment.  Indeed, if \(b(a)\ge1/4\) and \(f\) is any density supported on \(\mathcal A\), then Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(1=\int_{\mathcal A}f\le\sqrt{2B_A}\|f\|_2\), and hence
\[
 \|fb\|_{H^\beta}\ge\|fb\|_2
 \ge\frac14\|f\|_2
 \ge\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2B_A}}.
\]
Consequently the requested inequality \(\|fb\|_{H^\beta}\le R_q-\varepsilon_R\) requires \(R_q>1/(4\sqrt{2B_A})\), whereas primitive compatibility assumes only \(R_q>0\).

Conditional on compatible strict-interior fixed nuisances, moment annihilation gives analytic attenuation.  Put \(h_n=f(b_{1,n}-b_{0,n})\), and suppose that
\[
 \int_{\mathcal A}a^kh_n(a)\,da=0,
 \quad 0\le k<K_n.
\]
For \(|u|\le\Omega\), Taylor's formula, \(|a|\le B_A\), and the cancellations yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat h_n(u)|
 &=\left|\int_{\mathcal A}
 \left(e^{iua}-\sum_{k=0}^{K_n-1}\frac{(iua)^k}{k!}\right)
 h_n(a)\,da\right|\\
 &\le\|h_n\|_1e^{B_A\Omega}
       \frac{(B_A\Omega)^{K_n}}{K_n!}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The marked-channel factorization makes the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the observed marked perturbation equal to
\[
 \widehat h_n(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
\]
For fixed error transforms supported in bounded frequency intervals, this transform is confined to a fixed square and inherits the factorial bound.  What remains unproved is a packet that simultaneously preserves the Bernoulli range and strict Sobolev slack, attains \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) supremum separation, and admits a weighted chi-square or Hellinger inequality strong enough to imply the required product-experiment total-variation bound.
